"NC-A Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION {82.8ÆL HON. CARLOS G. DOMINGUEZ, 111 Secretary DOF Bldg., BSP Complex, Roxas Blvd., 1004 Metro Manila, Philippines Dear Secretary Dominguez, III: S. 20!A This has reference to your letter dated 4 November 2019, requesting the Department's legal opinion concerning the proposed ordinance of Malaybalay City, Bukidnon, entitled "AN ORDINANCE REGULATING THE OPERATION AND EXPANSION OF LARGE SCALE AGRI-INDUSTRIAL PLANTATIONS WITHIN THE CITY OF MALAYBALAY, DECLARING CERTAIN ACTS PROHIBITED AND PROVIDING PENALTIES, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES" Perusal of herein subject proposed Ordinance in question, it can be gleaned that the same seeks to regulate the operation and expansion of large scale agri- industrial plantations within the jurisdiction of herein concerned Sangguniang Panlungsod. The whereas clauses thereof essentially state the reason d'etre of its enactment. Among its key provision are: I. Section 4. Slope Limitation- Areas or portions thereof to be contracted by Large Scale Agri-industrial Plantations for pineapple, banana and commercial crop plantations exceeding 15% slope gradient shall not be utilized for production purposes. This area(s) may however be used as buffer zones for environmental impact mitigation purposes. Forest Fruit and Commercial Tree Plantations will be allowed in areas with slope gradient above 15%. Existing areas or portions which has a slope gradient greater than 15% should not be recultivated 5 years after the effectivity of this ordinance; 2. Section 11. Ban on Aerial Spraying- A ban on aerial spraying as an agricultural practice in all agricultural entities shall be strictly enforced in the territorial jurisdiction of Malaybalay City immediately after the effectivity of this Ordinance; 3. Section 12. Non-Conversion of Irrigated and Irrigable Areas- To ensure rice sufficiency, conversion of irrigated and irrigable area to Large Scale Agri-Industrial Plantations •is prohibited. All existing plantations

within irrigated and irrigable areas shall stop operations after 5 years upon effectivity of this Ordinance; and 4. Section 15. Implementation of Outreach Programs- As part of their corporate social responsibility, all Agri-Industrial Plantation Company shall conduct annual Outreach Program such as but not limited to Medical Mission, Feeding, Livelihood Assistance, and Educational Support Program to each of the barangay where the operation of the industry is located. Communities and residents surrounding the plantations shall be given priority as recipients of the CSR. Programs and activities under the CSR shall be included in the Annual Work Plan of the company indication the budget allocation. upon the foregoing premises, the Pilipino Banana Growers & Exporters Association, Inc. (PBGEA) manifested its opposition thereto in its letter addressed to the concemed Sangguniang Panlungsod on the grounds, inter alia, that the subject proposed ordinance usurps the functions of various national government agencies; that the proposed slope limitations are not grounded on actual farm practices; that the ban on aerial spraying is unconstitutional; that the closure of agricultural plantations on irrigated/irrigable farm lands is tantamount to unlawful taking; and that the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities must not be made mandatory; In essence, it is this Department's understanding that ultimately, herein issue hinges on the validity and legality of the subject proposed ordinance. Foremost, Local Government Units (LGUs), like the Sangguniang Panlungsod of Malaybalay, Bukidnon are vested by the Local Government Code the power to legislate for the general welfare of their constituents. Section 458 (a) of the Code provides, viz: "The sangguniang panlungsod, as the legislative body of the city, shall enact ordinances, approve resolutions and appropriate funds for the general welfare of the city and its inhabitants pursuant to Section 16 of this Code and in the proper exercise of the corporate powers of the city as provided for under Section 22 of this Code Section 16 of the Code provides that: "Every local govemment unit shall exercise the powers expressly granted, those necessarily implied therefrom, as well as powers necessary, appropriate, or incidental for iG emcient and effective govemance, and those which are esential to the promotion of the general welfare, Within their respective territorial jurisdictions, local govemment units shall ensure and support, among other things, the preservation and enrichment of culture, promote health and safety, enhance the right of the people to a balanced ecology, encourage and support the development of

appropriate and self-reliant scientific and technological capabilities, improve public morals, enhance economic prosperity and social justice, promote full employment among their residents, maintain peace and order, and preserve the comfort and convenience of their inhabitants. " Accordingly, we opine that herein concerned Sangguniang Panlungsod has the authority to enact an ordinance that seeks to protect the health and well-being of its constituents. It bears stressing, however, that an ordinance enacted by virtue of the genera/ welfare clause is valid, unless it contravenes the fundamental law of the Philippine Islands, or an Act of the Philippine Legislature, or unless it is against public policy, or is unreasonable, oppressive, partial, discriminating, or in derogation of common right. " In De Ia Cruz vs. Paraz, we laid the genera/ rule "that ordinances passed by virtue of the implied power found in the genera/ welfare clause must be reasonable, consonant with the genera/ powers and purposes of the corporation, and not inconsistent with the laws or policy of the State.l To address the issue on the legality and validity of herein subject proposed Ordinance, please be apprised that the Supreme Court (SC) had established a test in determining the validity and constitutionality of a local ordinance. In the case of City of Manila vs. Laguio, Jr. (G.R. No. 118127), the SC had elucidated the same, thusly: "xxx for an ordinance to be valid, it must not only be within the corporate powers of the local government unit to enact and must be passed according to the procedure prescribed by law, it must also conform to the following substantive requirements: (1) must not contravene the Constitution or any statute; (2) must not be unfair or oppressive; (3) must not be partial or discriminatory; (4) must not prohibit but may regulate trade; (5) must be genera/ and consistent with public policy; and (6) must not be unreasonable. Anent the first criterion, ordinances shall only be valid when they are not contrary to the Constitution and to the laws. The Ordinance must satisfy two requirements: it must pass muster under the test of constitutionality and the test of consistency with the prevailing laws. That ordinances should be constitutional uphold the principle of the supremacy of the Constitution. The requirement that the enactment must not violate existing law gives stress to the precept that local government units are able to legislate only by virtue of their derivative legislative power, a delegation of legislative power from the national legislature. The delegate cannot be superior to the principal or exercise powers higher than those of the latter. " 1 CITY OF BATANGAS vs. PHILIPPINE SHELL PETROLEUM CORPORATION and SHELL PHILIPPINES EXPLORATION B.V (G.R. NO. 195003

On this, allow us to discuss first Section II of the subject proposed Ordinance. Essentially, the same pursues the imposition of the ban against aerial spraying in all agricultural lands within Malaybalay City. It is noteworthy to mention that "Aerial Spraying" as defined therein, refer to application of substances through the use of aircraft of any form which dispenses the substances in the air. As can be discerned therefrom, it prohibits the aerial spraying per se, regardless of the substance of the level of concentration of the chemicals to be applied aerially. Herein issue appears to be parallel to the decided case of Wifredo Mosqueda, et,al, vs. PGBEA, Davao Fruits Corporation and Lapanday Agricultural and Development Corporation (G.R. No. 189185) wherein in the Supreme Court had this to say: "It can be noted that the imposition of the ban is too broad because the ordinance applies irrespective of the substance to be aerially applied and irrespective of the agricultural activity to be conducted. The respondents admit that they aerially treat their plantations not only with pesticides but also vitamins and other substances. The imposition of the ban against aerial spraying of substances other than fungicides and regardles of the agricultural activity being performed becomes unreasonable inasmuch as it patently bears no relation to the purported inØnvenience, discomfort, health risk and environmental danger which the odinance, seeks to addres- The burden now will become more onerous to various entities including the respondents and even others with no connection whatsoever to the intended purpose of the ordinance. Xxx" (Emphasis supplied) Hence, a ban on aerial spraying as provided in Section 11 of herein proposed Ordinance, renders nugatory the decision of the Supreme Court as above-cited. As such, we concur with the PBGEA's position that Section II of the subject proposed Ordinance is unreasonable. As regard Section 4 of the subject proposed Ordinance insofar as the proposed slope limitation is concerned, PBGEA contends that there Is no basis for setting slope limitation of greater than 15% for agricultural activities and is therefore unconstitutional. On this, please be apprised that pursuant to the Mapping Guidebook for Forest Land Use Plan of the Philippine Environmental Governance 2 Project, areas with 0-18% slope are suitable for agricultural and extensive agriculture practices. Thus, we are of the considered view that such limitation appears to be valid. Anent Section 12 of the subject proposed Ordinance, as above-mentioned, we deemed it proper that the same be referred to the Department of Agriculture (DA), the agency which has technical expertise on the matter. Finally, Section 15 thereof requires all Agri-Industrial Plantation Company to conduct annual outreach program to each of the barangay where the operation of the Industry is located. On this, may we note that nowhere in the Local Government Code

and its Implementing Rules and Regulations or in any other existing laws can we find a provision that empowers Local Government Units, like the herein concerned Sangguniang Panlungsod, to mandate companies to conduct outreach program as part of their corporate social responsibility. As such, CSR activities and programs should remain voluntary in nature. Notwithstanding the foregoing Opinion, this Department would like to emphasize that it has no power to invalidate the approved ordinance. Hence, we suggest that the same be filed in a proper forum. We hope the foregoing be sufficient to enlighten you on the matters presented herein. Please be reminded however that our opinion is without prejudice to the opinion of the higher authorities. cc: Thank you. E AR Sec ATTY. ODILON PASARABA Director, BLGS MR. STEPHEN A.
